title: A Multimodal Approach to Identify Metallothionein Metal Inducers in Nile Tilapia: Insights From Molecular Docking and Hepatocyte Exposure.
authors: da Luz, Jessica Zablocki; de Souza, Tugstenio Lima; de Almeida Roque, Aliciane; de Marchi, Micheli; Pozzan, Roberta; Confortin, Camila; Opuskevitch, Iracema; da Silva Ferreira, Fernando Cesar Alves; de Oliveira Ribeiro, Ciro Alberto; Neto, Francisco Filipak
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和肝细胞暴露实验评估金属对尼罗罗非鱼金属硫蛋白的诱导，虽涉及金属转录因子与MRE的互作背景，但核心是金属毒性生物标志物而非TF-DNA结合建模，方法仅简单对接，深度不足。
abstract: Many human activities contribute to the pollution of aquatic ecosystems, primarily through agricultural, industrial, mining, and domestic discharges into water bodies. Fish, being highly sensitive to environmental changes, serve as valuable models for monitoring the health of these ecosystems. Metallothionein (Mt), a biomarker for metal contamination, shows variable expression depending on the metal involved. Transcription of the mt gene is regulated by intracellular metal concentrations and mediated by interactions between metal-responsive transcription factors (Mtf) and metal response elements (MRE) in the mt promoter. Zinc plays a key role by binding to Mtf, activating it, and enabling interaction with MRE sequences to initiate transcription. In this context, this study aimed to identify the most potent inducers of mt expression in Oreochromis niloticus. Initially, zinc-binding proteins from O. niloticus were modeled to assess differential binding scores of various metals using molecular docking, which suggested the potency ranking Cd(2+) > Cu(2+) > Mn(2+) > Hg(2+) > Pb(2+). These predictions were validated using primary hepatocytes exposed to concentrations 10 times higher than the maximum allowed for effluent discharge under Brazilian law. The expression of both mt mRNA and Mt protein was evaluated in hepatocytes. Both in silico and in vitro results identified cadmium as the most potent inducer of Mt. Other metals did not induce mt expression under the tested conditions. These findings underscore the importance of understanding how Mt expression varies by metal and tissue, as differences in responsiveness can influence the interpretation of Mt levels in teleost fish used for water quality monitoring and environmental toxicology.
abstract_zh: 许多人类活动通过农业、工业、采矿和家庭排放进入水体，导致水生生态系统污染。鱼类对环境变化高度敏感，因此成为监测这些生态系统健康的重要模型。金属硫蛋白 (Metallothionein, Mt) 作为金属污染的生物标志物，其表达因涉及的金属不同而有所变化。mt基因的转录受细胞内金属浓度调控，并通过金属响应转录因子 (metal-responsive transcription factors, Mtf) 与mt启动子中金属响应元件 (metal response elements, MRE) 之间的相互作用介导。锌通过结合Mtf发挥关键作用，激活该因子并使其与MRE序列相互作用以启动转录。在此背景下，本研究旨在鉴定尼罗罗非鱼 (Oreochromis niloticus) 中mt表达的最强诱导物。首先，对O. niloticus的锌结合蛋白进行建模，利用分子对接 (molecular docking) 评估不同金属的差异结合分数，结果表明效力排序为Cd(2+) > Cu(2+) > Mn(2+) > Hg(2+) > Pb(2+)。这些预测通过暴露于巴西法律允许的废水排放最大浓度10倍的原代肝细胞进行验证。在肝细胞中评估了mt mRNA和Mt蛋白的表达。体外模拟和体外实验结果均表明镉是Mt的最强诱导物。在测试条件下，其他金属未诱导mt表达。这些发现强调了理解Mt表达如何随金属和组织变化的重要性，因为响应性差异可能影响对用于水质监测和环境毒理学的硬骨鱼类中Mt水平解读。
